newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB sees yr growth up, but demand pressured.
newsitem.headline: SAB sees yr growth up, but demand pressured.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd said on Wednesday that the lack of hoped-for interest rate cuts and volatility in financial markets would continue to undermine consumer confidence and strain disposable income.

"Notwithstanding these pressures, and providing consumer demand does not weaken significantly, the group should still achieve real growth in earnings and dividends for the year as a whole," the company said in a statement with half-year results.

The firm earlier posted half year results that just pipped analysts' expectations. The period saw earnings per share of 185.2 cents, up from 162.5, and a dividend hiked to 65 cents a share from 57 cents.
The firm said an unusually cold winter had not prevented growth at the firm's beer operations -- which saw earnings rise 17 percent on a modest increase in sales.
The firm's fast developing international beer division saw earnings up 26 percent.
The group recently launched a $413 million international share issue to raise funds for its overseas expansion. The group has interests in southern Africa, central and eastern Europe and China.
Analysts had been slightly nervous about the results as some of SAB's operations outside its beer businesses had been showing signs of faltering.

Lower-than-expected interim earnings reports from retailer Edgars Stores, Coca-Cola bottler ABI and glass-maker Plate Glass and Shatterprufe Industries Ltd, were all seen cutting into SAB's bottomline.
SAB said a weakening in the South African economy over the period had seen private consumption spending fall and hit consumer-orientated businesses.

"Nevertheless, the extent of SAB's broadly-based consumer interests ensured that the level of turnover, aided by international expansion, exceeded 17 billion rand for the year, reflecting growth of 16 percent," the firm said.
The group's competitive markets saw margins fall across the group, but the firm said it benefitted from tight cost control and a fall in its effective tax rate.
